items.notes: Explains the monthly budget as a residual allowance and the long-window dilution, then prescribes paired long/short burn windows with tiered actions; all six core claims are addressed with specific anchors.

Explains why interface conformance cannot carry failure, consistency and capacity semantics, then specifies the widened adapter contract and concurrency, loss, latency and version-skew tests covering the core claims.

Shows last-write-wins is a total order rather than a conflict contract, traces the tombstone and reconciliation resurrection, and treats synchronous multi-master as coordination cost with explicit rejection conditions; all six core claims are covered, though one inline atlas anchor (4472c6e0...) is not repeated in the citation array.

Separates the conservation census from per-request assignment and names the timeout, stale-event, boundary, event-order, retry-amplification and replay checks that cover the outcome path, addressing all five core claims.

Treats insufficient-evidence with recommendation none as a complete outcome, identifies forced recommendation and recommendation by default as the named failure modes, and explains the hidden measurement agenda and evidence-inflation alternatives.
